newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Chinese Petroleum Jan profit up.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Chinese Petroleum Jan profit up.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Tuesday it had reported a pre-tax profit of T$308 million in January, compared with December's loss of T$1.323 billion.

But the figure was still well short of a targetted T$2.01 billion for January despite an average nine percent domestic price increase on petroleum products that took effect on January 1, a company statement showed.
Chinese Petroleum's January oil import costs averaged US$22.62 per barrel, much higher than a budgeted US$15.26 per barrel, the statement said.
The firm has an accumulated deficit of T$12.746 billion from its July to January budget.
The oil monopoly had targetted a profit of T$20.5 billion during the 1996/97 (July-June) financial year.

Under strong pressure to alleviate growing budgetary shortfalls, Chinese Petroleum petitioned the government in December for an increase and was granted permission for an average nine percent rise, effective on January 1.
The government also agreed to let Chinese Petroleum raise local oil prices further -- but by no more than three percent -- three months after the January increase. ($1 = T$27.5)
